did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jeremiah 50 is a prophecy concerning Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, centered on the announcement of the Babylonian Empire’s fall.
Did you know? The prophecy mentions Bel and Merodach by name, the gods of Babylon, and presents their downfall as part of Babylon’s humiliation.
Did you know? The chapter describes the people of Israel and Judah returning together, weeping and seeking the LORD their God.
Did you know? The returning people ask the way to Zion and join themselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten.
Did you know? Babylon’s enemy is described as a great assembly of nations coming from the land of the north, and the archers are portrayed as warriors who do not return empty-handed.
Did you know? In this chapter, Israel is compared to a scattered sheep: the king of Assyria devoured it first, and Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon attacked it afterward.
Did you know? Alongside Babylon’s judgment, the LORD promises to restore Israel to its homeland, including Carmel, Bashan, the hill country of Ephraim, and Gilead.
Did you know? The chapter promises that in days to come, the sins of Israel and the offenses of Judah will be sought but not found, because the LORD will forgive the remnant he preserves.
Did you know? Babylon is called “the hammer of the whole earth,” but that very hammer will be cut down and shattered, becoming a horror among the nations.

Did you know? At the end of the chapter, the enemy against Babylon is compared to a lion rising from the thickets of the Jordan, and the prophecy emphasizes that no one can stand before the LORD or resist his counsel.
